item.title: Chinese participating troops arrive in Cambodia for exercise Golden Dragon-2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 -- China-Cambodia "Golden Dragon 2026" will be held from late November to mid-December in Cambodia. The Chinese participating troops and equipment have arrived in Cambodia in the last few days. The exercise focuses on joint counter-terrorism, anti-piracy, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) operations, and consists of adaptive training, command post exercises, and live-troop comprehensive drills. (Video Editor: Chen Zhuo)

item.title: China-Vietnam "Cooperation-2026" joint counter-terrorism training wraps up
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 -- The China-Vietnam "Cooperation-2026" joint counter-terrorism training successfully concluded in Hanoi, Vietnam, in recent days. Against the backdrop of jointly addressing terrorist threats and themed on jointly combating terrorist crimes, the joint training incorporated elements such as individual combat skills training, tactical coordination training, and comprehensive counter-terrorism exercises. Both sides conducted joint live-force drills including explosive ordnance disposal (EOD), battlefield first-aid operations, and counter-terrorism strikes in mountainous terrain. (Video Editor: Liu Sen)

item.title: Xi, Pakistani president exchange congratulations over joint spaceflight mission
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari exchanged congratulations on Wednesday on the joint spaceflight mission carried out by astronauts from the two countries. In his message, Xi said the joint space exploration of astronauts from China and Pakistan is a vivid embodiment of the deep-rooted friendship between the two countries, as well as another important achievement in bilateral cooperation. Xi said China stands ready to work with Pakistan and other countries to champion peaceful use of outer space and deepen space cooperation.

item.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 spaceship to Tiangong space station with first foreign astronaut on board
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasts off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Nov. 25, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Minggang) JIUQUAN, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- China launched the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship on Wednesday, sending three astronauts, including a Pakistani payload specialist, to its orbiting Tiangong space station. The spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China. The astronauts aboard the spaceship are mission commander and spacecraft pilot Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first-ever foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong. The Shenzhou-24 mission marks the first joint flight consisting of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program. item.title: China urges Japan to correct its remarks and actions on Taiwan question
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
China's Foreign Ministry on Friday urged Japan to correct its erroneous remarks and actions on the Taiwan question as soon as possible, stressing that Tokyo must honor its political commitments in both words and deeds. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun made the remarks at a regular press briefing in response to a question from a reporter about Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's comments about Taiwan following the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday. Takaichi said Japan's basic position on the Taiwan question remained consistent with the 1972 Japan-China Joint Communique, and that the positioning of the four political documents between the two countries as the foundation of bilateral relations had not changed. In response, Guo said Japan's adherence to the four political documents between China and Japan was a political responsibility and legal obligation that it must fulfill. This commitment should be reflected not only in its statements but also in its actions, he added. "For Japan, the pressing task now is to correct its erroneous remarks and actions on the Taiwan question as soon as possible. What is important is to adopt a correct attitude toward historical issues, and what is fundamental is to develop a truly objective and rational understanding of China," Guo said.

item.title: China-Russia-U.S. summit to discuss global peace
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
BEIJING, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- The heads of state of China, Russia and the United States will have an in-depth exchange of views on important issues concerning global peace in their upcoming summit, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Wednesday. Guo made the remarks at a regular news briefing when asked about the trilateral leaders' summit in China's Shenzhen on Nov. 19.
